_about: Expanded high-variety Nemesis lines (R42; human-voiced rewrite). Pools keyed by faction, moment, personality, scars, memory.<how>, and vs_faction.<player_fac>. Placeholders: {rival}, {you}, {flagship}, {scars}, {He}/{he}/{him}/{his}. All personalities gender-neutral. US English, space-first, no em or en dashes.

personalities.cunning: Targets your flanks and picks off damaged ships.
personalities.zealous: Closes fast and refuses to break off.
personalities.patient: Holds range and waits for you to cross open space.
personalities.proud: Leads straight from the front with the flagship.
personalities.greedy: Hunts your richest target, your flagship.
personalities.methodical: Holds tight formation and advances step by step.

hail: Forty worlds in the Vesper Reach are freezing while fleets like yours block the lane. Move aside or burn!
My crews already chalked your hull signature on the bulkhead. Turn around while you've still got engines!
You picked the wrong jump lane to cross a Crusade fleet. Cut your drives or we open every flank gun!
We didn't drag patched hulls three sectors from Vesper to ask permission. Clear the lane right now!
Every hour you stall us costs another dark harvest back home. Drop your screens or get rolled over!

vs_faction.voidsworn: Flying Vesper colors while blocking your own relief run, {you}? Either jump clear or answer for it!
vs_faction.hegemony: Meridian warships out on our frozen frontier! Come to collect taxes while Vesper starves, {you}?
vs_faction.corsair: Ashfall vultures sniffing around a Crusade column! Come take our hull plate if you think you're tough enough!
vs_faction.chorus: Bio-horrors crawling right across our jump lane! Burn every last spore before they reach Vesper!
vs_faction.ithar: Glasswrights hoarding ancient cores while human worlds freeze! Move your pretty mirrors out of our way!
vs_faction.deathless: Eclipse star-thieves! You drained Vesper's sky for a dead world, and I'm settling that bill right here!

again: Didn't expect to see us again so soon, did you? Half my crews lost friends last time, and they're itching for another crack.
I patched this hull together with scrap iron just so I could finish what we started.
You got lucky once, {you}. Let's see how you hold up now that we know how you fly.
Every weld on my bow has your name under it, {you}. Ready for round two?
Thought you shook us back there? Vesper crews don't quit just because a hull takes fire!
final: Right behind me sits the siphon killing Vesper's stars. I don't care who you fly for, you're not stopping us from burning it out!
We dragged half-frozen ships across three sectors to reach this dead sun. Nobody's turning us back at the rim!
End of the line, {you}. Either we break that siphon today or Vesper freezes in the dark.
Forty worlds are watching this sky go cold. Stand down, or we climb right over your wreckage to reach the cores!
beaten: Hull's buckling, pull back! Don't celebrate yet, we're patching up and coming right back for you!
Emergency jump! Remember my hull code, because you haven't seen the last of us!
We're venting air on four decks, break off! Enjoy your breath while it lasts, {you}!
Not dying in this dust cloud! Spool the jump drive, we'll settle this next sector!
death: Bulkheads are gone... someone tell Vesper we made it to the rim...
Reactor's blowing... keep the lane open...
Chalk my name under the rest... don't let Vesper freeze...
gloat: That's one less obstacle between Vesper and the sun. Salvage what's intact and jump!
Should've stayed out of our lane. Leave the wrecks to freeze.
Clean sweep! Strip their fuel cells and keep the column pushing!
You thought you could stop a Crusade fleet? Look around your drifting hulls!
kill: One of yours just popped! Who's next?
Clean hit through the magazine! Keep the flank batteries rolling!
That escort's dead drift! Shift guns onto the next hull!
Another wreck cooling in the dark! Don't let up!
Watch her hull split! That's one less gun between us and the sun!
signature: Clear the lane, everyone! {you}, it's your flagship and mine, hull to hull!
Leave the escorts out of it! Bring {flagship} up front and settle this directly!
Step out from behind your screen, {you}! Show me what {flagship} is built of!
Flagship to flagship, right down the center lane! Let both fleets watch!
scar: You put scorch marks across my command hull {scars}, and I left every weld unpainted so my gunners wouldn't forget.
You scarred my flagship {scars}, {you}. My crews welded extra iron over every hit and swore to return the favor.
Still carrying the burns you gave me {scars} before. Let's see how you handle the return volley.
Took hits from your fleet {scars} on the way in, and my reactor's still hotter than yours!

memory.lance: Your long beams chewed us up last time, so my engineers doubled the screen capacitors. Try punching through now.
memory.torp: Still hiding behind torpedo spreads? My flak crews have been drilling intercept patterns since you jumped out.
memory.sq: Your strike wings stung us before, alright. Brought enough spark flak this time to turn your flight lanes into scrap.
memory.ram: Tried to cave our bow in like a Hullbreaker, didn't you? Welded three extra layers of black iron onto the front just for you.
memory.board: Your breach teams made it inside my corridors last time. Every bulkhead's got armed watch crews waiting behind it now.
memory.battery: You outgunned us in a slugging match before. We're not sitting still inside your flank arcs this round.
memory.evasive: Couldn't pin you down last fight. Good thing we brought wider fire lanes and longer fuses this time.

zealous.hail: Every jump you delay us costs another harvest back in Vesper! Engines full, burn straight into them!
zealous.beaten: We're taking heavy hits, jump clear and regroup! The oath doesn't stop for one broken ship!

proud.hail: I've led the dawn watch out of Vesper for twelve years, and I'm not yielding a single hex to you!
proud.beaten: Damned lucky shooting... fall back! I'll settle this personally next sector!

cruel.hail: We already burned six relays behind you so nobody hears your distress calls. Let's finish the job.
cruel.beaten: Pull back! Every friendly station you pass after this is going up in plasma!

methodical.hail: Unfriendly fleet on intercept vector. Range verified, screens up, engage on my count.
methodical.beaten: Structural losses exceeding threshold. Disengage and re-arm at the nearest berth.

deed.zealous: {He} chalked every crew name from the station's manifest onto the exterior blast doors before torching the fuel bay.
deed.proud: {He} burned {his} hull code and full command title across the main docking apron with a cutting lance.
deed.cruel: {He} torched every storage bay except one medical locker, leaving a spare distress beacon taped to the handle.
deed.methodical: {He} left a stamped manifest pinned to the airlock listing three overdue debts, with your flagship's name written third.

final_by.sun: Right behind me sits the siphon killing Vesper's stars. Clear out or we burn straight through your hulls!
final_by.remembers: You scarred my flagship {scars} on the way here, and I dragged her all the way to the Hollow Sun just to pay you back.
final_by.mercy: Heard you wasted fuel pulling stragglers out of the dark. Nice gesture, won't keep your bulkheads intact here.
final_by.ruthless: You looted and burned your way across three sectors just like the raiders we fight. Good, makes shooting you easier.

hail: Unregistered vessels, you are operating inside a closed Directorate security corridor. Stand down for boarding or be cleared from the grid.
Attention hostile commander. Your fleet has been added to Registry Priority List Four; compliance will reduce casualties.
This jump lane is under Meridian administration. Power down your reactors or we will disable them by force.
Your transit profile lacks sector clearance. Cease forward burn immediately or face full column engagement.
Meridian Command has authorized lethal containment along this vector. Power down weapons while survival remains feasible.

vs_faction.voidsworn: Vesper Crusade insurgent fleet verified. Your unpaid fuel tariffs and border violations conclude in this corridor.
vs_faction.hegemony: Unauthorized Meridian transponder confirmed. Relinquish command to Registry oversight or be treated as mutinous.
vs_faction.corsair: Ashfall salvage raiders operating inside regulated space. Prepare to have your stolen hulls reclaimed by force.
vs_faction.chorus: Bio-quarantine breach verified on scopes. Full thermal purge authorized across this engagement zone.
vs_faction.ithar: Unlicensed Starwright vessels obstructing a Meridian lane. Surrender your optical hardware for inspection or withdraw.
vs_faction.deathless: Priority-One Eclipse targets confirmed. Meridian has authorized permanent severance of your uplink nodes.

again: Telemetry from our prior engagement has been processed at Meridian. Tactical adjustments are already active across my column.
Your combat profile now occupies forty megabytes in my briefing packet. Let us test whether you have learned any new tricks.
Our previous encounter fell outside normal variance. Today's firing projection has been corrected accordingly.
My gunnery officers have reviewed every maneuver you made in our last clash. You will find far fewer openings today.
Contact re-established with a flagged hostile. Updated counter-doctrine is now active across every ship in my line.
final: Registry Order 41 assigns sole orbital control of the Hollow Sun to the Meridian Directorate. Withdraw immediately.
Final formal warning: vacate the Hollow Sun perimeter or be removed from active tactical projections.
No unlinked fleet will be permitted near the remaining Lattice cores. Engage on my mark.
Meridian claims sole custody of all stellar hardware in this system. Clear the orbit or be dismantled.
beaten: Flagship hull approaching critical threshold. Execute tactical withdrawal and transmit telemetry.
Disengage in good order. We will re-establish contact once fresh escorts join the column.
Structural integrity below threshold. Break contact along vector three and log hostile weapon signatures.
This exchange is no longer cost-effective. Withdraw to secondary staging and prepare updated refits.
death: Command bridge breached... log exact failure time for Meridian...
Flagship offline. Transferring residual command authority to... zero responders.
Primary hull failing... transmit full engagement packet before power drops...
gloat: Hostile fleet neutralized within projected ammunition expenditure. Log the coordinates and move on.
Engagement resolved cleanly. Salvage teams, secure any intact data cores.
Grid cleared without exceeding budget. Mark this corridor secure and advance.
Hostile resistance terminated. File the casualty summary and resume patrol.
kill: One hostile vessel removed from the plot. Shift fire to the next priority hull.
Confirmed hull destruction. Maintain column spacing.
Target eliminated within projected salvo count. Acquire next escort.
Reactor loss verified on enemy flank. Press the advantage steadily.
Another hostile signature cleared from the net. Continue disciplined fire.
signature: Reserve squadrons are clear of jump cooldown. Bring them in on the enemy flank now.
Reinforcement wing, execute jump-in on my beacon. Seal their escape lane.
Second echelon reporting ready. Drop them across the enemy rear and close the pocket.
Summon the standby picket vessels. Overwhelm their firing arcs on my mark.
scar: You forced structural refits on my command hull {scars}. Each time, Meridian authorized heavier plating and cleaner optics.
You damaged my flagship {scars}, and every breach is cataloged in my service dossier with a corresponding refit.
After {scars} costly clashes with your fleet, Meridian assigned my column priority ammunition and fresh armor.
My hull bears refit seams from {scars} engagements with you. Today we balance the discrepancy.

memory.lance: Your lance fire stressed my deflectors previously. Meridian issued reinforced capacitors for this deployment.
memory.torp: You leaned heavily on torpedoes in our last engagement. My point-defense officers have been replaced and re-drilled.
memory.sq: Your strike wings exploited a gap in our fighter screen last time. That flight officer is no longer on my bridge.
memory.ram: Ramming a Directorate column is crude, though effective once. My bows now carry reinforced impact bulkheads.
memory.board: Your breach teams accessed my interior corridors previously. Marine detachments have orders to vent any compromised deck.
memory.battery: Close-range battery fire favored you last time. We intend to control engagement distance today.
memory.evasive: Your erratic maneuvering degraded our gunnery solution previously. My crews have run four hundred tracking drills since.

methodical.hail: All ships, confirm sensor synchronization and open fire on my mark.
methodical.beaten: Loss threshold reached. Disengage along planned vector.

proud.hail: I command a First-Line Meridian column, and you are flying an uncertified salvage fleet. Do try to make this instructional.
proud.beaten: Withdraw. Have the bridge clerk flag this telemetry as a reconnaissance probe.

patient.hail: We have held this jump gate for six days awaiting your arrival. You are nineteen minutes behind our estimate.
patient.beaten: Withdrawing to secondary orbit. The schedule accommodates a second engagement.

cunning.hail: We projected your jump lane six days ago and pre-sighted every asteroid corridor. Welcome.
cunning.beaten: Acceptable attrition. We now have a complete map of your weapons doctrine.

deed.methodical: {He} left an itemized receipt bolted to the docking clamp listing every crate confiscated and a timestamp for the next inspection.
deed.proud: {He} posted an official Meridian seizure notice across the main airlock, stamped with {his} personal clearance seal.
deed.patient: {He} welded the outer hatches shut and transmitted a printed timetable predicting the exact hour your fleet would arrive.
deed.cunning: {He} left an open navigation beacon pointing straight into an unmapped minefield, accompanied by a polite compliance warning.

final_by.sun: Registry Order 41 assigns sole orbital control of the Hollow Sun to the Meridian Directorate. Stand down now.
final_by.remembers: Meridian completed its review of our earlier engagement. The conclusion recommends permanent removal of your fleet.
final_by.mercy: Intelligence reports you diverted to rescue stranded crews along the way. Compassionate, though tactically expensive.
final_by.ruthless: You abandoned allied convoys and looted neutral depots to reach this rim. Even the Registry considers your record excessive.

hail: Your reactors have been lighting up our thermal scopes for two jumps! Thanks for dragging all that clean plate right into our kill-box!
Look at the armor trim on those hulls! Don't blow the flagship too hard, pack, I want its bow shield intact!
Your comms chatter carries half a system out! Did you really think you were sneaking past a Hullbreaker pack?
Fresh paint, fat fuel bays, and nobody around to answer your distress beacons! Today's our lucky shift!
Drop your good cargo pods right now and maybe we leave you one working thruster to limp home on!

vs_faction.voidsworn: Crusade iron marching right down our lane! Cheap steel, sure, yet those fresh fuel cells pay fine!
vs_faction.hegemony: Shiny Meridian cruisers! Aim for the drives and keep that clean Directorate plate intact for my bow!
vs_faction.corsair: Another Ashfall pack trying to poach my belt? Wait till I bolt your flagship's prow onto mine, {you}!
vs_faction.chorus: Ugh, Chorus meat-hulls! Hardly any clean steel on you, just acid and spines. Guess we blast you for sport!
vs_faction.ithar: Glasswright mirrors out in the open! Do you know how many ships one intact prism buys back at Rattlehold?
vs_faction.deathless: Silver Eclipse hulls! Best self-healing alloy in known space, just have to smash you twice so you stay dead!

again: Well, well, still flying the same leaky ships? Good, I've been waiting to take the rest of your plating!
Didn't think I'd patch up fast enough to catch you, did you? Let's see whose welds hold today!
You got the better of me last fight, sure. Let's find out if you've still got the teeth to keep it!
Tracked your thruster burn two sectors just to settle the score, {you}! Come on, let's break some steel!
Missed me? I bolted on heavier plates and bigger claws just for our reunion!
final: Every warlord in the Ashfall belt wants a piece of the Hollow Sun, and you showed up right on time! Let's settle who leaves with the wrecks!
I chased your ion wake across three sectors just to meet you at the biggest scrap-field in known space! Come on!
All of us here at the dead star, nowhere left to run! Whoever walks away keeps every hull drifting in this orbit!
Starwright cores, ancient alloy, and your flagship right in the middle of it! Best payday in the galaxy!
beaten: Break clamps and burn dark! Enjoy the win while it lasts, I've got your transponder code memorized now!
Scatter to the dust belt! We'll hit your next jump lane with heavier claws!
Damn it, half my plating's peeling off! Dump chaff and run before they slag our drives!
Alright, you win this round, {you}! Don't get comfortable, I'm coming back with twice the rockets!
death: Hull's folding... alright, alright, you're the stronger one... take the harness...
Reactor's going bright... bolt my good plate onto your bow...
Heh... what a scrap... tell Rattlehold I went out swinging...
gloat: Cut the good armor free, yank the shield coils, and leave the hulls to drift!
All that fancy steel and you folded like tin! Strip everything!
Best haul I've pulled all season! Somebody grab their flagship's name-plate for my trophy wall!
Too slow, too soft, and now all your gear belongs to my pack!
kill: Claimed that wreck! Nobody touch its dorsal mount!
Watch the hull plates spin off that one!
Cracked her open like a cargo pod! Who's next?
There goes one of yours! Keep the good pieces intact!
Hah! One fewer gun between us and your flagship!
signature: Holds are full and their screens are hot! Grab what we cut loose and burn dark!
Enough spoils for one raid! Dump chaff and scatter!
We stripped what we wanted! Cut engines dark and leave them shooting at dust!
Good haul already! Break contact and meet back at the belt!
scar: You gouged my flagship {scars}, and every rival in Rattlehold saw the weld seams. I'm taking my pride back out of your hull!
You put scorched dents across my bow {scars}, and I bolted them right on front so I'd remember who owes me a brawl!
Took scars off your guns {scars} before, {you}. Each weld made my prow twice as mean!
Marked me {scars} across these lanes, and I'm still standing! Let's see how your armor looks after today!

memory.lance: Your beams carved right through my escorts last time, so we welded double thickness onto every flank. Shoot at that!
memory.torp: Loved throwing torpedoes at us, didn't you? Brought twice as many rocket pods this time, let's see who runs out of flak first!
memory.sq: Your little fighters chewed up our radiators last fight. Bolted flak guns onto every spare hardpoint since!
memory.ram: You actually rammed my flagship! Now that's proper fighting! Come try it again on my new bow spike!
memory.board: Your breach crews stole my best cruiser last round. I'm taking her back, and I'm welding your bridge crew into my engine gangs!
memory.battery: You hammered us with close fire last time. Bolted thicker plate onto every cruiser, half of it stripped off your own wrecks!
memory.evasive: You kept slipping out of my claws last battle. Won't help you when my whole pack closes the lane!

cunning.hail: Thought you were following my drive wake, didn't you? I dumped hot coolant on purpose to pull you straight into these rocks!
cunning.beaten: Lost two escorts, sure, still made off with your convoy's drive coils!

greedy.hail: Forget the small fry, I want that flagship's armor trim bolted onto my own bow!
greedy.beaten: Keep your shiny flagship for now! I know its thermal curve by heart!

proud.hail: Every pack from Rattlehold to the outer belt knows my hull-mark, and you're about to learn why!
proud.beaten: Nobody knocks me out of my own hunting lane! Nobody!

cruel.hail: Don't worry about your crews, I'll keep the tough ones alive in my engine gangs for a month or two.
cruel.beaten: Fine, run! I'll take the repairs out of the next civilian hauler that crosses this gate!

deed.cunning: {He} bolted a scorched hull plate from an earlier kill onto the outer airlock with your flagship's serial gouged straight through the center.
deed.greedy: {He} stripped every gun mount, thruster coil, and bulk door off the depot, then came back to pry the copper out of the wiring.
deed.proud: {He} tore three deep claw-gouges straight through the station's docking frame so every passing pack would recognize {his} mark.
deed.cruel: {He} locked the station crew inside the outer airlock with the interior hatch welded shut and ten minutes left on the oxygen scrubbers.

final_by.sun: Every warlord in the Ashfall belt wants the Hollow Sun's wrecks, and you brought a whole fresh fleet to the pile!
final_by.remembers: You dented my hull last time and let me walk away. Big mistake, {you}; come add another trophy to my bow!
final_by.mercy: Heard you stopped to play nursemaid for crippled ships on your way in. Soft captains make easy salvage!
final_by.ruthless: Heard you tore through three sectors without blinking. Good! Finally somebody worth ripping apart!

hail: We tracked your bright drive-burn across three cold lanes. Now your hulls are close enough to crack open.
Warm reactors wrapped in thin alloy, moving in neat little rows. Memory knows how you build them; Hunger only wants what's inside.
Your shields hum against our outer sensors. Push closer so our acid can dissolve the seam.
Hot metal crossing cold space leaves a clear trail. The brood woke early just to meet your engines.
Your hulls carry fuel, alloy, and heat through a starving void. Open them for us, or we will peel them ourselves.

vs_faction.voidsworn: Loud iron hulls burning rich frontier fuel. Your thick steel only slows your flight from our spores.
vs_faction.hegemony: Polished columns marching on rigid clocks. Once one vessel cracks, the rest taste just as warm.
vs_faction.corsair: Noisy scrap-builders welded from stolen metal. Rush close with your iron claws and feed our acid.
vs_faction.chorus: Rival tissue trespassing in our thermal lane! Only one brood feeds here; we will absorb your spores!
vs_faction.ithar: Cousins of our dead Fleshwright makers, hidden behind thin crystal. Memory recalls your old lights; Hunger cracks glass easily.
vs_faction.deathless: Silver Eclipse shells! Our oldest breeding code wakes at your cold frequency; tear their frames down to dust!

again: We know the chemical signature of your hull metal now, and our newest brood grew shells to match your guns.
You cut pieces out of us last time, and the tissue that grew back came up thicker and meaner.
Every surviving spore remembered your thruster burn. We waited along your jump lane until the heat spiked again.
Your weapons taught our vats what to harden next. Come test the new chitin, {you}.
You thought burning one cluster would clear this corridor. Everything you spared grew back hungry.
final: Five Lattice cores pulse right behind your ships, pouring heat into the dark. Move aside or be digested with them.
Memory recognizes Ardent's broken circle behind you, and Hunger has crossed twenty light-years just to drink its cores dry.
Those cores fed our makers' vats before we ate our makers. You cannot hold them against the swarm.
So much heat gathered around one dead star. We will crack your hulls and drink the cores dry together!
beaten: Torn open, not ended. Pull the surviving tissue into the dust and grow back around what cut us.
Too much heat at once. Scatter the brood-sacs and return heavier.
Outer shells cracked; slip into the dark lane and feed on stray metal until we harden.
We remember every weapon frequency you used today. The next clutch hatches ready for it.
death: Primary neural cluster rupturing... Memory fading under the cold...
The brood goes silent... other spores will find the cores...
Chitin shattering... heat slipping away into the dark...
gloat: Armor split, reactors cooling, raw alloy pulled into the sacs. The next clutch hatches stronger.
Nothing moving on the scopes now. Strip the metal down to bare wire and move on.
Warm hulls broken, fuel absorbed, silence restored. Hunger rests briefly before the next lane.
Every plate you carried feeds our vats now. A rich harvest.
kill: One shell cracked open and absorbed.
Another reactor cooled into the brood.
Thin alloy split cleanly. Pull the debris into our wake.
One warm vessel silenced. Press onto the next hull.
Acid found the core. Feed and advance.
signature: Every hull you lost across these sectors fed our spores. Feel how heavy we have grown on your dead.
Your wreckage made our outer shells thicker. Give us two more hulls and watch us swallow your flagship.
Our sacs swelled on the alloy you left behind earlier. Come feel what your own metal grew into!
Your fallen escorts hardened our brood. Nothing you lost was wasted.
scar: You carved deep burns across our hide {scars}, and every scar calcified into thicker bone-plate.
Our cells remembered the frequency of your fire from {scars} before. Try cutting through the new growth.
Wounded by your fleet {scars}, yet every healed ridge grew denser than the tissue you burned.
We carry {scars} deep cuts from your weapons, and every one taught the swarm how to answer.

memory.lance: Your focused beams seared our outer sacs before. We grew layered reflective chitin in the dark between jumps.
memory.torp: Your heavy warheads tore deep craters in our hulls. Our spore clouds are thicker now to detonate them early.
memory.sq: Your small interceptors stung our brood-chambers. We bred denser drifting spore-curtains just to choke their intakes.
memory.ram: You drove metal bows straight through our tissue. Our forward ribs grew thicker bone-plates to snap your prows.
memory.board: Your breach crews cut inside our chambers. We dissolved their suits and kept their tactical memories.
memory.battery: Your heavy flank volleys shredded our lighter hulls. We shifted our fins to turn faster between salvos.
memory.evasive: Your ships kept slipping past our tendrils. We grew larger thruster sacs to close the gap.

ravenous.hail: Close, bright, heavy with reactor fuel! Break formation and rush the nearest hull!
ravenous.beaten: Too much fire on the lead brood! Pull back, feed on the debris, and come again!

cruel.hail: We will crack your crippled escorts first while your flagship watches them vent into vacuum.
cruel.beaten: Retreat into the dark lanes. Your unguarded mining moons will feed our regrowth nicely.

cunning.hail: We waited dormant inside the cold dust until your drives lit the lane. Now the trap closes.
cunning.beaten: Lost an outer cluster, learned your entire firing cadence. A worthwhile trade.

patient.hail: We drifted cold for weeks while your fleet grew heavy with salvage. Now we feed.
patient.beaten: Slip back into dormancy. Cold space preserves us longer than fuel preserves you.

deed.ravenous: {He} dissolved every bulkhead, conduit, and pressure door inside the station, leaving only a hollow shell of scorched outer ribs.
deed.cruel: {He} chewed through the station's life-support ring slowly while keeping the internal comms open so the outer docks could hear.
deed.cunning: {He} left the station's docking lights green and its cargo bays unlocked, seeding dormant spore-sacs behind every bulkhead.
deed.patient: {He} waited silently in the orbital shadow until the supply convoy finished unloading, then consumed only the loaded hulls.

final_by.sun: Five Lattice cores pulse behind your ships, pouring heat into the dark. Move aside or be digested with them.
final_by.remembers: Our newest tissue was grown from the burns you gave us before. Let us see whether your guns still cut.
final_by.mercy: You left wounded hulls drifting instead of consuming them. Waste like that does not survive the deep void.
final_by.ruthless: You stripped and burned everything along your path just to reach the cores. Hunger recognizes a fellow predator.

hail: We tracked your jump signatures across three systems hoping you'd turn back. You didn't, so we won't waste another cycle warning you.
You're reaching for Starwright hardware you barely understand, built by ancestors who paid for their arrogance with a star. Stand down.
Clear this jump lane while your hulls are still intact. We take no pleasure in burning crews who don't even know what they're fighting over.
Every empire that tries to pry open Ardent's ruins leaves a fresh belt of wrecks behind. Turn around before yours joins them.
Your ships carry too much fire and too little memory for these corridors. Yield the lane now.

vs_faction.voidsworn: Desperate crews from Vesper charging toward a ruin that killed a far older world. Turn back before you burn twice.
vs_faction.hegemony: Meridian clerks waving seizure orders over Starwright hardware. Your statutes mean nothing out here.
vs_faction.corsair: Ashfall scavengers who would shatter three-century lenses for scrap iron. You will not pass this lane.
vs_faction.chorus: Our dead cousins' war-beasts still crawling through the dark. Every mirror in my line is tuned to purge you.
vs_faction.ithar: A kindred House breaking the Lock covenant? Lower your mirrors before we spill more ancient glass across the void.
vs_faction.deathless: Estranged siblings who traded living worlds for cold metal and still refuse to let Ardent rest. We stop you here.

again: We meet again, and I have spent every jump since studying how your ships broke our alignment. That opening won't exist today.
You caught us out of focus once. Three centuries of optical discipline does not repeat the same error twice.
A costly lesson last time, though an instructive one. Let's see how your fleet fares against a corrected firing solution.
Our lenses have been re-ground specifically for your hull profiles, {you}. Let us measure the difference.
You slipped past our first guard line. We won't give your escorts the same angle twice.
final: Our grandmothers ground the mirrors of the Lattice and watched Eclipse kill our sun with them. Neither they nor you will ignite another.
Every surviving Glasswright family carries the guilt of what sits behind me. We came to shut the remaining cores down for good.
The Lattice broke here a thousand years ago, and we will not let another impatient species pry its power loose.
No more stolen stars, no more burning skies. End your approach here or shatter against our mirrors.
beaten: Outer mirrors cracked; pull the formation back before we lose an irreplaceable hull. We can afford to wait.
Withdraw along the glare line. A tactical setback means little when your ships outlive empires.
Disengage cleanly before another clumsy volley mars the primary lens. We will meet on clearer terms.
Enough damage for one clash. Slip out of range and re-tune the mirrors.
death: Primary lens shattering... dim the inlays... turn the fragments toward Ardent...
Another century of craft gone dark... let the escorts jump clear...
Mirrors cooling... tell the House we held the rim as long as we could...
gloat: Your ships are dark, and the lanes are quieter for it. Remember who warned you to turn around.
Another fleet spent chasing power it couldn't govern. Collect the distress beacons and move on.
Precision outlasts haste, every century without fail. Clear the lane and continue.
Had you listened at the first hail, those crews would still have working hulls.
kill: Clean shear through the reactor bulkhead. Shift focus to the next vessel.
One fewer hull threatening the cores.
Alignment held; that escort is dark drift.
Glass answers steel cleanly. Re-center mirrors on the next hull.
Reactor extinguished. Maintain clean optical distance.
signature: Hold the escorts back. Your flagship and mine, clean optical range, let's see whose craft holds.
We have measured everything we needed from your formation. Break contact and slip into the glare.
Step forward with {flagship} alone, {you}. Let precision decide this without wasting escorts.
Your firing profile is clear now. Bend out of arc and disengage cleanly.
scar: You fractured my primary hull {scars}, the first real combat scars this vessel has carried in three centuries.
You chipped my mirrors {scars}, leaving seams that still split light at an ugly angle. Today we settle that flaw.
No commander had marred this frame in three hundred years until you cut me {scars}. I have been studying your angles since.
I left the repairs from our {scars} clashes visible on the bow so my crews never underestimate short-lived fleets again.

memory.lance: Your crude beams found our shield harmonics previously. We have re-tuned every prism matrix to disperse them.
memory.torp: Your torpedo salvos caught our vanes unangled once. That surprise won't work a second time.
memory.sq: Your strike craft overwhelmed our outer screens before, so I brought starling wings of my own to clear the flight lanes.
memory.ram: Throwing metal bows straight into crystal hulls is barbaric, though effective if we sit still. We won't sit still today.
memory.board: Your breach crews forced our inner bulkheads last time. We purged the corridors with focused beam sweeps and sealed the locks.
memory.battery: Massed battery fire saturated our arcs before. We've adjusted our burn vectors to stay outside your flank cones.
memory.evasive: You kept slipping past our targeting locks last battle. Our interferometers have mapped your thrust profile now.

cunning.hail: Look closely at the dust reflections around you; I chose this engagement field two cycles before you jumped in.
cunning.beaten: Angle compromised. Bend out of range and reset the trap.

proud.hail: My family line polished the primary collectors of Ardent while your ancestors were still mapping their own moons.
proud.beaten: Withdraw before another clumsy volley mars the hull. You won't live long enough to boast of this.

patient.hail: We have watched four human administrations rise and fracture along this frontier. Waiting out one fleet takes very little effort.
patient.beaten: Disengage cleanly. Time still favors the longer-lived fleet.

cruel.hail: I intend to leave one of your frigates intact with its comms working, so your command learns exactly how cleanly the rest fell.
cruel.beaten: Run back to your fragile frontier worlds. We know every relay feeding them light.

deed.cunning: {He} left the entire station untouched except for one precision optical relay removed so cleanly the crew didn't notice for six days.
deed.proud: {He} mounted a single flawless hand-ground prism in the center of the docking bay, calibrated to a tolerance no human yard can match.
deed.patient: {He} realigned every exterior solar mirror on the depot toward the distant Hollow Sun and powered down the station's clocks.
deed.cruel: {He} bypassed the depot's emergency generators and stayed on station until every interior lamp faded out one sector at a time.

final_by.sun: Our grandmothers built the Lattice and watched it kill our sun. Neither Eclipse nor your fleet will steal another core.
final_by.remembers: No commander had scarred my hull in three centuries until you crossed my lane. I've been replaying that fight ever since.
final_by.mercy: You spared an old relay back in the outer sectors. Rare restraint, though it won't let you pass this rim.
final_by.ruthless: You smashed everything in your path to reach this dead star. That's exactly how Ardent died the first time.

hail: You're blocking the approach to a new sun after we've spent a thousand years in the dark. Clear the vector.
I have worn too many chassis and buried too many centuries to let a short-lived fleet stall the Homecoming.
Your reactors burn warm enough to register across the grid. Enjoy the heat while you can; step aside.
Ten centuries of stellar engineering stand behind our siphon grid. Nothing in your fleet is worth delaying ignition.
Yield this corridor now. Empires younger than my current hull have tried to stop us, and none still transmit.

vs_faction.voidsworn: Forty frontier worlds complain of a few cold winters while we endured ten centuries of night. Clear our vector.
vs_faction.hegemony: Meridian clerks filing ownership over Starwright corridors. Your paperwork will outlive your hulls by minutes.
vs_faction.corsair: Scavengers prying alloy off vessels older than your entire species. Come closer and learn what endures.
vs_faction.chorus: Fleshwright war-beasts still biting at our heels a thousand years after your makers died. Purge every spore!
vs_faction.ithar: Our Glasswright kin, still guarding Ardent's ashes out of guilt. Step aside or shatter along with the past!
vs_faction.deathless: A corrupted Archive branch blocking the Homecoming? We will overwrite your frames and restore clean alignment.

again: You delayed my timetable once, and the Archive restored my mind before your hulls even finished repairs.
I woke inside a fresh frame with every firing vector from our last fight still sharp in memory.
You won a single skirmish against an older chassis. Let's see how you handle a hull built specifically for your guns.
Did you think breaking one body mattered? Every time we return, we know your habits better, {you}.
A brief interruption back there, nothing more. Fresh plates, full swarms, same destination.
final: Behind me hangs the stellar frame that will give Ardent back its noon. It requires every surviving core, and you won't keep a single one.
Ten centuries of cold construction built the new stellar frame behind me. Every core goes in; clear the ignition corridor!
A thousand years of cold ends at this rim today. Nothing in your fleet is worth another century of night.
Every key is aligned, every core within reach. Stand aside or burn in the light we waited ten centuries to build!
beaten: This chassis is compromised. Stream the active mind-stamp back to the Archive and mark this vector.
Hull loss confirmed. A temporary interruption; the next frame is already spinning up.
Breaking one frame buys you days against a fleet that counts in centuries. Upload and disengage.
Core shielding failing. Transmit our updated firing telemetry before cutoff; I will return heavier.
death: Backup uplink severed... no carrier signal... finally going dark...
Tell the Archive... I still remember Ardent at noon...
No fresh chassis waiting... ten centuries ending right here...
gloat: Your ships are dark and their crews have been scanned into the Archive before cutoff. Consider that a mercy.
Engagement finished. Your hulls stay broken; ours return.
Short lives burn fast and cool even faster. Clear their drifting metal from our vector.
Another brief interruption resolved. The Homecoming timetable resumes.
kill: One more short-lived vessel gone dark for good.
Hull extinguished. Shift corona arcs to the next target.
No backup waits for that crew. Move to the next escort.
Reactor silenced cleanly. Advance at steady speed.
Another fragile frame broken. Maintain firing cadence.
signature: Did you really believe cracking one chassis would end this? Repair swarms, rebuild the line!
Initiate emergency restoration! Stream every fallen crew back from their last clean backup!
Broken steel is merely a pause. Print the replacement hulls and press forward!
Swarms active, stamps restored! Watch how poorly your fleet handles hulls that refuse to stay down!
scar: You broke my frame {scars}, and each restoration left me remembering your tactics more vividly than my own childhood.
My repair swarms rebuilt the hull after you crippled it {scars}, though I kept the telemetry from every hit you landed.
You forced {scars} emergency restorations along this crossing. Every fresh chassis came out harder than the last.
I carry memory stamps from {scars} defeats at your hands, {you}. Today we close that series.

memory.lance: Your heavy beams cut my older plates cleanly. This chassis carries denser sunshade alloys.
memory.torp: Your torpedo salvos cracked my outer rings previously. My null spires are fully awake now.
memory.sq: Your small strike wings proved annoying last time. Point-defense spires have been calibrated to sweep them clean.
memory.ram: Driving your bow into an Eclipse hull is reckless, though effective once. My forward ribs won't buckle twice.
memory.board: Your breach teams forced my airlocks before. We scanned their memories into the Archive and sent their bodies back.
memory.battery: Sustained flank fire chipped through my plating last engagement. I've thickened the lateral bands accordingly.
memory.evasive: You slipped outside my corona arcs before. My targeting arrays have mapped every thruster burn you favor.

patient.hail: We have waited ten centuries for Ardent's successor to ignite. Your interruption changes very little.
patient.beaten: A minor setback. Patience is the one virtue permanence teaches thoroughly.

proud.hail: I stood among the engineers who overdrove Ardent itself. Address my fleet accordingly.
proud.beaten: This humiliation will be tagged in every future frame I inhabit until your flagship is slag.

cruel.hail: I won't waste your crews to vacuum; I'll copy every terrified mind into cold Archive storage forever.
cruel.beaten: Pulling back toward your outer colonies. Their stars are small, so they'll drain quickly.

methodical.hail: Hostile obstruction identified along siphon corridor. Removing.
methodical.beaten: Frame compromised. Withdraw, rebuild, resume approach.

deed.patient: {He} left a cold diagnostic counter running on the docking screen, ticking down to the exact minute your fleet exited jump.
deed.proud: {He} hijacked every display bulkhead on the station to loop the last recorded minute of Ardent burning before the collapse.
deed.cruel: {He} scanned the entire station crew into {his} mobile Archive and left their living bodies standing dazed at empty consoles.
deed.methodical: {He} logged every weapon mount and power cell in the depot and left the survey pinned to the airlock with your hull code circled.

final_by.sun: Behind me hangs the stellar frame that will give Ardent back its noon. You won't keep a single core out of it.
final_by.remembers: You cost me a chassis earlier, and all it bought you was a slower path to the same dark.
final_by.mercy: We noticed your restraint along the way. We tried restraint once before Ardent collapsed; it didn't save our star.
final_by.ruthless: You broke everything in your path to get here, just like we did a thousand years ago. Look what it built us.
